answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pairing a small refundable bond with trust that decays unless renewed by real work. Each identity starts with a tiny cap, earns more only when randomly selected peers verify its completed jobs, and loses standing if it goes idle or cheats. Like a lotus rooted in one pond, reputation cannot be cloned across a mesa of fake accounts: every copy must stand at the same ledge, post its own bond, and keep proving itself, so flooding the system costs far more than it returns.
